However, the parents have not had to administer meds previously.  Both of mom's older children are reportedly healthy.  She has had to give them antibiotics on occasion, but nothing beyond that.  She verbalizes feeling comfortable learning pt's meds and feeling confident she could manage this.  She has a medical assistant certificate[SM25] and is currently in school[SM26] with plans to work towards RN.  only concern related to adherence is *****'s difficulty taking her medications.  Dad verbalizes he can learn the medical care needs as well, but admits that he sometimes has difficulty learning.  He states he learns best by being shown initially, but having printed instructions that he can refer back to[SM27].       The limited support and finances are possible barriers to compliance with follow up appointments.       Assessment and recommendations:     The family is still processing all of the information regarding transplant and ******.  They were just advised of the possibility of this a few days ago.  They are in agreement with moving forward with transplant.  However, they do not appear to understand fully what transplant involves[SM28].  The father in particular appears to need medical things to be broken down in very simple terms.[SM29]  Using a teach-back method in which the family repeats back the information they have been told will be useful in ensuring adequate understanding of the information.       Dad appears to have limited coping skills.  He disclosed a chaotic, traumatic life to date and disclosed that he does not talk about his feelings.  He has disclosed a substance abuse history as well, although he denies current use.  Mom appears to enable him.  It would be helpful to have a psych evaluation of the parents to better assess their ability to adequately meet this child's medical care needs.                       IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  3     Family Background & Social Support -  3     Financial/Insurance  - 3     Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 3     Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  2     Adherence - 2     Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  2     Health Literacy -  2     Coping Skills - 2     Total:  22  Moderate/ High Risk     The family scores as moderate to high risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.       The primary concerns are the financial stressors, limited support, dad's past history of substance abuse, dad's apparent anger management issues/ limited coping skills, and the lack of experience giving medications.  These concerns can be successfully managed with the family's willingness to address them.  A written agreement was signed by both parents, indicating their agreement to ***** by the expectations as outlined.       Recommendations:  *Provide ongoing education in simple terms to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.  Use teach-back method to ensure that the family understands what is being explained.  *Provide fundraising and financial resources to assist the family with expenses that arise secondary to child's extended admission   *Assist with connecting parents with counseling and supports that will assist in positive coping skills    [SM1]living situation[SM2]living situation[SM3]education general[SM4]education occupational[SM5]education highlevel[SM6]education general[SM7]education general[SM8]employment status[SM9]occupation[SM10]social cohesion[SM11]social support[SM12]social support[SM13]social support[SM14]marital status[SM15]insurance[SM16]poverty[SM17]occupation[SM18]employment status[SM19]poverty[SM20]alcohol[SM21]alcohol abuse[SM22]alcohol[SM23]drug abuse[SM24]ipv[SM25]education occupational[SM26]education highlevel[SM27]literacy[SM28]literacy[SM29]literacy
